items.title: As many as His creation
items.cue: The four phrases, said three times, that outweigh a morning of remembrance
items.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ عَدَدَ خَلْقِهِ وَرِضَا نَفْسِهِ وَزِنَةَ عَرْشِهِ وَمِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِ
items.transliteration: Subhaanallaahi wabihamdihi 'adada khalqihi waridaa nafsihi wazinata 'arshihi wamidaada kalimaatih
items.translation: Glory and praise be to Allah, as many as His creation, as much as pleases Him, the weight of His Throne, and the ink of His words.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sahih Muslim, ed. Muhammad Fu’ad Abd al-Baqi, hadith 2726: https://shamela.ws/book/1727/6846

witnesses.name: hadith-api
witnesses.ref: fawazahmed0/hadith-api, edition ara-muslim, hadith 2726 (comparison only)

usage.evidence: The Prophet ﷺ told Juwayriyah, after she had sat in remembrance from the dawn prayer until mid-morning, that he had said four phrases three times which would outweigh all she had said (Muslim 2726).

items.title: Asking for wellbeing
items.cue: The duas the Prophet ﷺ never left, morning and evening
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، اللَّهُمَّ أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي دِينِي وَدُنْيَايَ وَأَهْلِي وَمَالِي، اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عَوْرَاتِي، وَآمِنْ رَوْعَاتِي، وَاحْفَظْنِي مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيَّ، وَمِنْ خَلْفِي، وَعَنْ يَمِينِي، وَعَنْ شِمَالِي، وَمِنْ فَوْقِي، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أُغْتَالَ مِنْ تَحْتِي
items.transliteration: Allaahumma innee as'alukal-'afwa wal-'aafiyata fid-dunyaa wal-'aakhirah, allaahumma as'alukal-'afwa wal-'aafiyata fee deenee wadunyaaya wa'ahlee wamaalee, allaahummastur 'awraatee, wa'aamin raw'aatee, wahfaznee mim bayni yadayy, wamin khalfee, wa'an yameenee, wa'an shimaalee, wamin fawqee, wa'a'oodhu bika an ughtaala min tahtee
items.translation: O Allah, I ask You for pardon and wellbeing in this world and the next. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and wellbeing in my religion and my worldly life, my family and my wealth. O Allah, cover my faults and calm my fears, and guard me from in front of me and behind me, from my right and my left, and from above me; and I seek refuge with You from being seized unawares from beneath me.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sunan Ibn Majah, ed. Muhammad Fu’ad Abd al-Baqi, hadith 3871: https://shamela.ws/book/1198/5348

witnesses.name: hadith-api
witnesses.ref: fawazahmed0/hadith-api, edition ara-ibnmajah, hadith 3871 (comparison only)

provenance.note: The printed Abd al-Baqi text on Shamela has اللهم أسألك in the second sentence; hadith-api has اللهم إني أسألك. We follow the printed edition.

usage.evidence: Ibn Umar said the Prophet ﷺ never left these duas, evening and morning (Ibn Majah 3871; Abu Dawud 5074 relates it with small differences).

items.title: We have reached the evening
items.cue: "We have reached the evening, and the dominion belongs to Allah…"
items.arabic: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَخَيْرِ مَا فِيهَا، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا وَشَرِّ مَا فِيهَا، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَالْهَرَمِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ وَفِتْنَةِ الدُّنْيَا وَعَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ
items.transliteration: Amsaynaa wa'amsal-mulku lillaah, wal-hamdu lillaah, laa ilaha illallaahu wahdahu laa shareeka lah, allaahumma innee as'aluka min khayri hadhihil-laylati wakhayri maa feehaa, wa'a'oodhu bika min sharrihaa washarri maa feehaa, allaahumma innee a'oodhu bika minal-kasali wal-harami wasoo'il-kibari wafitnatid-dunyaa wa'adhaabil-qabr
items.translation: We have reached the evening, and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what is in it, and I seek refuge with You from its evil and the evil of what is in it. O Allah, I seek refuge with You from laziness, from decrepitude, from the misery of old age, from the trials of this world and from the punishment of the grave.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sahih Muslim, ed. Muhammad Fu’ad Abd al-Baqi, hadith 2723: https://shamela.ws/book/1727/6841

witnesses.name: hadith-api
witnesses.ref: fawazahmed0/hadith-api, edition ara-muslim, hadith 2723 (comparison only)

when: Evening; in the morning with its opening changed
usage.evidence: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reports that the Prophet ﷺ said this in the evening (Muslim 2723, the narration of Za'idah). Another narration under the same number adds, after "without partner", His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things; and says that in the morning he opened with "We have reached the morning".

variants.label: In the morning he said the same, opening with these words.

items.title: Knower of the unseen
items.cue: What the Prophet ﷺ taught Abu Bakr for morning, evening and bedtime
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ فَاطِرَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ، رَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَمَلِيكَهُ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ نَفْسِي، وَشَرِّ الشَّيْطَانِ وَشِرْكِهِ
items.transliteration: Allaahumma faatiras-samawaati wal-ard, 'aalimal-ghaybi wash-shahaadah, rabba kulli shay'in wamaleekah, ashhadu an laa ilaha illaa ant, a'oodhu bika min sharri nafsee, washarrish-shaytaani washirkih
items.translation: O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord and Sovereign of everything: I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek refuge with You from the evil of my own self, and from the evil of Satan and his call to associate others with You.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sunan Abi Dawud, ed. Muhyi al-Din Abd al-Hamid, hadith 5067: https://shamela.ws/book/1726/6927

witnesses.name: hadith-api
witnesses.ref: fawazahmed0/hadith-api, edition ara-abudawud, hadith 5067 (comparison only)

usage.evidence: Abu Bakr asked for words to say morning and evening; the Prophet ﷺ taught him these and said: say it in the morning, in the evening and when you lie down (Abu Dawud 5067). Al-Tirmidhi relates it with the first two phrases in the other order (3392) and calls it hasan sahih.

items.title: By You we enter the morning
items.cue: "O Allah, by You we enter the morning…"
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا، وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ
items.transliteration: Allaahumma bika asbahnaa, wabika amsaynaa, wabika nahyaa, wabika namoot, wa'ilaykan-nushoor
items.translation: O Allah, by You we reach morning and by You evening; by You we live and die, and to You is the rising.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sunan Abi Dawud, ed. Muhyi al-Din Abd al-Hamid, hadith 5068: https://shamela.ws/book/1726/6928

witnesses.name: hadith-api
witnesses.ref: fawazahmed0/hadith-api, edition ara-abudawud, hadith 5068 (comparison only)

when: Morning; the evening wording is shown under it
usage.evidence: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet ﷺ said this on reaching the morning, and the shorter wording on reaching the evening (Abu Dawud 5068). Al-Tirmidhi relates it with إليك المصير in the morning wording (3391) and calls it hasan.

variants.label: In the evening: "O Allah, by You we enter the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the rising."
variants.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ

items.title: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing harms
items.cue: The protection said three times morning and evening
items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ، وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
items.transliteration: Bismillaahi lladhee laa yadurru ma'asmihi shay'un fil-ardi walaa fis-samaa'i, wahuwas-samee'ul-'aleem
items.translation: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing in the earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sunan Abi Dawud, ed. Muhyi al-Din Abd al-Hamid, hadith 5088: https://shamela.ws/book/1726/6948

witnesses.name: hadith-api
witnesses.ref: fawazahmed0/hadith-api, edition ara-abudawud, hadith 5088 (comparison only)

usage.evidence: Uthman reports the Prophet ﷺ saying that whoever says it three times in the evening will not be struck by sudden calamity until morning, and whoever says it three times in the morning, not until evening (Abu Dawud 5088; al-Tirmidhi 3388).

items.title: Al-Falaq
items.cue: Seeking refuge with the Lord of daybreak, three times morning and evening

usage.evidence: Abdullah ibn Khubayb reports that the Prophet ﷺ told him to say Qul huwa Allahu ahad and the two Mu'awwidhat three times in the evening and the morning, and they would suffice him against everything (Abu Dawud 5082; al-Tirmidhi 3575, who says: hasan sahih gharib).

items.title: Al-Ikhlas
items.cue: The surah of pure oneness, said three times morning and evening

usage.evidence: Abdullah ibn Khubayb reports that the Prophet ﷺ told him to say Qul huwa Allahu ahad and the two Mu'awwidhat three times in the evening and the morning, and they would suffice him against everything (Abu Dawud 5082; al-Tirmidhi 3575, who says: hasan sahih gharib).

items.title: The perfect words of Allah
items.cue: What to say in the evening for protection from harm
items.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
items.transliteration: A'oodhu bikalimaatillaahit-taammaati min sharri maa khalaq
items.translation: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sahih Muslim, ed. Muhammad Fu’ad Abd al-Baqi, hadith 2709: https://shamela.ws/book/1727/6814

witnesses.name: hadith-api
witnesses.ref: fawazahmed0/hadith-api, edition ara-muslim, hadith 2709 (comparison only)

usage.evidence: A man stung by a scorpion came to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: had you said this when evening came, it would not have harmed you (Muslim 2709).

items.title: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah, a hundred times
items.cue: Said a hundred times in a day
items.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
items.transliteration: Laa ilaha illallaahu wahdahu laa shareeka lah, lahul-mulku walahul-hamd, wahuwa 'alaa kulli shay'in qadeer
items.translation: There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari, al-Sultaniyya print, hadith 6403: https://shamela.ws/book/1681/9610

witnesses.name: hadith-api
witnesses.ref: fawazahmed0/hadith-api, edition ara-bukhari, hadith 6403 (comparison only)

usage.evidence: Whoever says it a hundred times in a day, it is for him like freeing ten slaves, a hundred good deeds are written for him and a hundred bad deeds wiped away, and it is a protection for him from Satan that day until evening (al-Bukhari 6403; Muslim 2691).

items.title: An-Nas
items.cue: Seeking refuge with the Lord of people, three times morning and evening

usage.evidence: Abdullah ibn Khubayb reports that the Prophet ﷺ told him to say Qul huwa Allahu ahad and the two Mu'awwidhat three times in the evening and the morning, and they would suffice him against everything (Abu Dawud 5082; al-Tirmidhi 3575, who says: hasan sahih gharib).

items.title: The best way to ask forgiveness
items.cue: "You are my Lord, there is no god but You…"
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ بِذَنْبِي، اغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
items.transliteration: Allaahumma anta rabbee, laa ilaha illaa ant, khalaqtanee wa'anaa 'abduk, wa'anaa 'alaa 'ahdika wawa'dika mastata't, a'oodhu bika min sharri maa sana't, aboo'u laka bini'matika 'alayy, wa'aboo'u bidhanbee, ighfir lee, fa'innahu laa yaghfirudh-dhunooba illaa ant
items.translation: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep to Your covenant and Your promise as far as I am able. I seek refuge with You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge to You Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin. Forgive me, for no one forgives sins but You.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari, al-Sultaniyya print, hadith 6306: https://shamela.ws/book/1681/9452

witnesses.name: hadith-api
witnesses.ref: fawazahmed0/hadith-api, edition ara-bukhari, hadith 6306 (comparison only)

provenance.note: The printed al-Sultaniyya text on Shamela reads وأبوء بذنبي، اغفر لي; hadith-api reads وأبوء لك بذنبي، فاغفر لي. We follow the printed edition.

usage.evidence: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever says it by day, certain of it, and dies that day before evening, is among the people of Paradise; and the same for whoever says it by night and dies before morning (al-Bukhari 6306).

items.title: Glory and praise, a hundred times
items.cue: Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi, a hundred times morning and evening
items.translation: Glory and praise be to Allah.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sahih Muslim, ed. Muhammad Fu’ad Abd al-Baqi, hadith 2692: https://shamela.ws/book/1727/6778

witnesses.name: hadith-api
witnesses.ref: fawazahmed0/hadith-api, edition ara-muslim, hadith 2692 (comparison only)

usage.evidence: Whoever says it a hundred times on reaching the morning and the evening, no one will bring anything better on the Day of Resurrection except one who said as much or more (Muslim 2692).
